caliber

Monotone calibration of a digital or performance measure to a multi-item PRO. One latent trait drives the PRO items (graded response model, items scored 0 to 3) and the digital measure (non-increasing cubic B-spline mean, log-linear residual SD). The curve is fitted by monotonic likelihood boosting (Leitenstorfer and Tutz 2007) in three ways: MS-Fixed (fixed-item calibration, the recommended primary analysis), MS-Joint (concurrent calibration) and MS-EAP (EAP plug-in, the naive comparator).

The curve can instead be fitted with Ramsay’s (1988) monotone regression splines (fit_ms(..., curve = "ispline")): a non-negative combination of I-splines on a few interior knots at quantiles of the latent N(0, 1), fitted by maximum likelihood, with the number of knots chosen by AIC. Boosting stays the default.

Install (from this folder) 

install.packages(c("mirt", "statmod", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "scales", "viridisLite"))
roxygen2::roxygenise(".")      # builds man/ (and checks NAMESPACE)
devtools::install(".")         # or: R CMD build . && R CMD INSTALL caliber_0.1.0.tar.gz

Main functions

Step Functions
GRM on the PRO fit_grm()
Curve fit_ms() (curve = "boost" or "ispline"), fit_three(), mu_sqi(), sigma_sqi(), ispline_basis(), ispline_knots()
Interpretation threshold_locations(), threshold_flags(), crosswalk(), crosswalk_probabilistic(), exceedance_probabilistic(), curve_ends(), plausible_values()
Intervals ms_vcov() + ms_intervals() (items, thresholds, crosswalk), ms_bootstrap() + boot_intervals() (curve)
Figures wright_map_sqi(), plot_expected_scores()
Example data psqi_sleep, pf_gait (data sets); sleep_data(), sleep_eta_true(), simulate_sleep_data(), gait_data()

Data sets

Both are lazy-loaded (caliber::psqi_sleep, caliber::pf_gait) and documented in ?caliber::psqi_sleep and ?caliber::pf_gait. data-raw/datasets.R rebuilds them from the CSV files in data-raw/.

Data set Rows × columns Content
psqi_sleep 1000 × 11 Simulated PSQI components C1–C7, PSQI global, actigraphy SQI and the true trait eta_true; simulate_sleep_data(seed = 20261003)
pf_gait 1426 × 15 NHANES 2001–2002 (MSX_B, PFQ_B, DEMO_B), ages 60+, gait speed and seven mobility items; built by inst/scripts/gait_data.R, unweighted

Documentation

Rendered vignettes and the function reference are in docs/ (pkgdown site), served at https://paoloeusebi.github.io/caliber/ when GitHub Pages is enabled for main / docs.

The digital measure is called sqi in the code (from the sleep example); any measure that falls as the latent trait rises can be used.

Examples

Vignettes: vignette("sleep-simulation", "caliber"), vignette("nhanes-gait", "caliber"). Full analyses (write to $CALIBER_OUT, default output/):

Script What it does Environment variables
sleep_step1.R Three approaches on the sleep data, bootstrap MS_BOOT (200), MS_DRAWS (2000), MS_HETERO (1), MS_CORES
sleep_simulation.R 6 scenarios × 200 replications MS_REPS, MS_DRAWS (0), MS_HETERO, MS_CORES
sleep_simulation_summary.R Tables and figures of the simulation MS_HETERO
gait_data.R Builds the gait analysis file from NHANES XPT files NHANES_DIR
gait_dimensionality.R Dimensionality and local-dependence checks (needs lavaan) as gait_main
gait_main.R Gait example, bootstrap, figures GAIT_BOOT (200), GAIT_CORES, GAIT_EXCL_AIDS, GAIT_SKIP_UNABLE

Find them with system.file("scripts", package = "caliber").

Caveats

Neither the normal-approximation intervals nor the curve bootstrap has been validated by a coverage simulation. The normal-approximation draws condition on the selected boosting path and understate the curve’s variance, so curve bands come from the bootstrap only.

The reported results of the manuscript were produced by the project scripts of 8 October (sleep) and 11 October (gait), before this package. With MS_DRAWS = 0 the package scripts should reproduce them; CHECK_NOTES.md records whether that was confirmed.
